items.descriptionOriginal: One of the great things about America is that we have a relatively young culture, so many of the foods that we eat were brought over from other countries . That makes America a great place to try out all the different types of food from around the world. However, we also like to put our own stamp on staples from around the globe that give the American version its own unique flair. Some foods that we claim originated overseas were actually first made right here in the U.S. of A. For example, chimichangas, which can be found in many Mexican restaurants, most likely originated in the state of Arizona. Crab Rangoon, a popular “Chinese” dish, is believed to have been created in the San Francisco Bay area, and spaghetti and meatballs is largely an Italian-American creation. The video that broke the internet TikTok creator Gabby Donahue posted a video that’s the perfect example of how some ethnic foods get remixed once they become popular in the States. In a video with over 7 million views, her father shows a waiter in Italy a photo of chicken parmesan from Olive Garden so he can order it at the restaurant. The waiter’s reaction is an excellent example of someone trying to be polite while he cannot believe what he is seeing. “My Boston Irish father trying to order a Google image of the Olive Garden chicken parm in Italy ,” Donahue wrote in the text overlay. When the father showed the picture to the waiter, he seemed a bit confused about the image. “Only in the States,” he said. “It doesn’t exist in Italy.” The father couldn’t believe what he was hearing: “It doesn’t exist in Italy?” “I don’t know what it is… on the pasta?” the waiter said, trying to make sense of the chicken breast smothered in cheese and sauce. The waiter gave his final verdict while holding his chin: “No. That’s horrible.” “Horrible? Wow. Look at that. That doesn’t,” the father laughed. “That looks good… but,” the waiter shrugged off the father. “It does look good,” the father continued. “It tastes good. I’ll tell you what, I’m gonna mail you some. I’ll send it to you.” “Okay? Olive Garden chicken, I’m gonna search,” the waiter said, walking away from the table. The commenters had a field day analyzing the waiter’s body language. “‘No, that looks good’ while looking completely disgusted was the most Italian reaction ever,” one commenter wrote. “Bro remembered halfway through his disgust that he’s at work,” another added. So where did chicken parm actually come from? It’s not crazy that an American would think that chicken parmesan is an Italian dish; after all, it’s served in most Italian-American restaurants. However, according to Paesana , it was created in America by the Italian diaspora. “In the Old World, that’s Italy prior to the Italian diaspora (the large-scale emigration of Italians from Italy to America), proteins like chicken were not widely available,” according to an article on the site. “As such, the prototypical chicken parmigiana was actually made with breaded, fried slices of eggplant in place of chicken for a dish called melanzane alla Parmigiana.” Even though chicken parmesan didn’t originate in the old country, Pasquale Sciarappa , a popular Italian-born food influencer living in America, has no problem cooking the dish. “‘That’s not Italian!’ I hear this every time I share a dish like Chicken Parmigiana. And you know what? They’re right. It’s not something you’d traditionally find in Italy. But you know what else is true? It’s Italian-American. It was born in immigrant kitchens from people who left Italy, landed in the U.S., and made do with what they had. They took inspiration from dishes like melanzane alla parmigiana and recreated comfort from memory using what was available,” he wrote. Watch Pasquale make his chicken parmesan: America’s food is a beautiful remix It’s understandable that an American could go to Italy without knowing that something he’d had in Italian restaurants wasn’t actually from Italy. It’s understandable for an Italian server to balk at a photo of a dish served in an American restaurant that you’d find in a shopping mall. But we should all agree that one of the wonderful things about American culture is that it’s an amalgamation of different cultures stirred around in the same pot, and if that means we get a fresh variation on the burrito, a new way to eat Chinese crab, or a tasty piece of chicken where eggplant used to be, the more the better. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post American orders Olive Garden-style chicken parm in Italy and the waiter’s response is perfect appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Σ τα 41 του χρόνια, δεν υποβάλλεται καν σε… «διαλειμματική νηστεία» από τα γκολ και τους πανηγυρισμούς τερμάτων, εξακολουθώντας να κάνει αυτό που γνωρίζει καλύτερα από σχεδόν οποιονδήποτε άλλο της γενιάς του: να σκοράρει και να εισπράττει αστρονομικά ποσά. Κι αυτό δεν είναι πρόσφατο. Δεν ξύπνησε ένα πρωί, στην εποχή του επικείμενου ποδοσφαιρικού του φινάλε, και αναρωτήθηκε: «Τι τα κάνω τόσα λεφτά που έχω;» Πάνε μπόλικα χρόνια, από την περασμένη δεκαετία, που τα γκολ του Ρονάλντο δεν αποτελούν αυτοσκοπό και λογίζονται ως το (πάγιο) τερπνό μετά του ωφέλιμου. Η διαρκής αποθέωση και ο θόρυβος της γηπεδικής λατρείας γύρω από το όνομά του είναι συνάμα το «καύσιμο» μιας δεύτερης καριέρας. Διότι ούτε το χρήμα ούτε και τη δόξα αγνόησε κανείς!.. Κι αν κάποτε το μεγάλο ερώτημα της διεθνούς στατιστικής ποδοσφαίρου ήταν πόσα ακόμη γκολ θα πετύχει, σήμερα υπάρχει ένα εξίσου ενδιαφέρον: Πόσα χρήματα μπορούν να γεννήσουν τα… χρήματα που κέρδισε παίζοντας ποδόσφαιρο; Τα κοκόρια του Κριστιάνο… γεννούν κι αυτό είναι σίγουρο. Χάρη σε ένα μυαλό όμως που δεν περιορίζεται, δεν αρκείται στην ανάδειξή του, απλώς, ως κροίσου της μπάλας αλλά η επενδυτική σκέψη του είναι τέτοια και τόση που τον ανακηρύσσει και σε πρωταθλητή στο επιχειρείν. Ο «νερουλάς» και τα πετροδόλαρα που χρηματοδοτούν το μέλλον Στην Μπραγκάνσα της Πορτογαλίας δημιουργείται μια μεγάλη μονάδα εμφιάλωσης νερού, συνολικής επένδυσης περίπου 20 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ, στην οποία ο Πορτογάλος star συμμετέχει κατά 50%, μαζί με τον πορτογαλικό όμιλο Outeirinho. Η δική του συμμετοχή αντιστοιχεί σε επενδυτικό μερίδιο περίπου 10 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ και η μονάδα προβλέπεται να λειτουργήσει στις αρχές του 2028, με δυνατότητα παραγωγής 500 έως 600 εκατομμυρίων λίτρων ετησίως και εξαγωγικό προσανατολισμό. Για τον… «νερουλά» Κριστιάνο, δεν είναι η πρώτη του επαφή με το συγκεκριμένο προϊόν. Το 2023 είχε ήδη παρουσιάσει το φυσικό μεταλλικό νερό «Ursu». Όμως, άλλο να εξαργυρώνεις επιχειρηματικά το πρόσωπό σου, παραχωρώντας το για να μπει σε μια ετικέτα, κι άλλο να επενδύεις στην παραγωγική υποδομή πίσω από αυτήν. Ο Ρονάλντο φαίνεται να ενδιαφέρεται ολοένα περισσότερο για το δεύτερο… Η οικονομική αφετηρία αυτής της επέκτασης βρίσκεται, ασφαλώς, και στη Σαουδική Αραβία. Η μεταγραφή του στην Αλ Νασρ, στα τέλη του 2022, υπήρξε μια από τις πιο εντυπωσιακές εμπορικές συμφωνίες στην ιστορία του αθλητισμού. Σύμφωνα με τις εκτιμήσεις του Forbes για το 2026, ο Ρονάλντο εισπράττει συνολικά 300 εκατομμύρια δολάρια ετησίως: 235 εκατομμύρια από το ποδόσφαιρο και άλλα 65 εκατομμύρια από χορηγίες, εμπορικές συμφωνίες και εξωαγωνιστικές δραστηριότητες. Μέσα σε δύο χρόνια οι συνολικές ετήσιες απολαβές του αυξήθηκαν κατά 40 εκατομμύρια δολάρια. Ακόμη πιο εντυπωσιακό: τα εξωαγωνιστικά έσοδα αυξήθηκαν κατά 30% μεταξύ 2025 και 2026… (άνω τελεία, μικρή παύση… αναπνοή!). Διαβάστε επίσης: Από τα εσώρουχα και τα ξενοδοχεία στις μετοχές Η επιχειρηματική ιστορία του δεν ξεκίνησε στη Σαουδική Αραβία. Το 2013 λανσάρισε την επωνυμία CR7 στην αγορά των εσωρούχων, επεκτείνοντάς την αργότερα σε ρούχα, υποδήματα και αρώματα. Ακολούθησε η συνεργασία με τον πορτογαλικό όμιλο Pestana και η δημιουργία των Pestana CR7 Lifestyle Hotels, με παρουσία από τη Λισαβόνα και τη Μαδέρα μέχρι τη Μαδρίτη, τη Νέα Υόρκη και το Μαρακές. Παράλληλα εισέβαλε και στον χώρο των κλινικών μεταμόσχευσης μαλλιών μέσω της Insparya, επεκτάθηκε στα media με τη Medialivre και απέκτησε επιχειρηματική συμμετοχή στον ιστορικό πορτογαλικό όμιλο πορσελάνης Vista Alegre. Όμως, οι πιο χαρακτηριστικές κινήσεις της νέας του στρατηγικής βρίσκονται αλλού: Το 2024 επένδυσε στην αμερικανική WHOOP, εταιρεία τεχνολογίας που αναπτύσσει φορητές συσκευές παρακολούθησης της φυσικής κατάστασης και της αποκατάστασης. Την ίδια χρονιά μπήκε στην Bioniq, εταιρεία εξατομικευμένων συμπληρωμάτων διατροφής, η οποία αποτιμήθηκε τότε στα 82 εκατομμύρια δολάρια. Ενώ τον Φεβρουάριο του 2026 επένδυσε 7,5 εκατομμύρια δολάρια για να αποκτήσει το 10% της HBL Pro2col Software, θυγατρικής της Herbalife. Αγοράζει ποδόσφαιρο και επενδύει στο Χόλιγουντ Σημειώστε από εδώ και πέρα: Τον Φεβρουάριο του 2026 ήρθε μια ακόμη κίνηση με ισχυρό συμβολισμό. Η απόκτηση του 25% της ισπανικής Αλμερίας, μέσω της CR7 Sports Investments. Τι κάνει, λοιπόν, πλέον ο Κριστιάνο, ο άνθρωπος που για δεκαετίες αποτελούσε το ακριβότερο περιουσιακό στοιχείο των συλλόγων του; Αρχίζει να αποκτά ο ίδιος συμμετοχές σε ποδοσφαιρικές ομάδες! Μαγκιά; Και επειδή το ποδόσφαιρο δεν είναι το μοναδικό θέαμα που παράγει χρήμα, το 2025 συνεργάστηκε με τον Βρετανό σκηνοθέτη Μάθιου Βον για τη δημιουργία εταιρείας κινηματογραφικών παραγωγών. Από τα γήπεδα στα κινηματογραφικά στούντιο. Και από εκεί στις τεχνολογικές εταιρείες, στις ξενοδοχειακές επιχειρήσεις και στη βιομηχανία τροφίμων και ποτών. Πώς είπατε; Διαβάστε επίσης: Η δημοσιότητα ως ισχυρό επιχειρηματικό κεφάλαιο Το 2025, ο Bloomberg Billionaires Index αποτίμησε την περιουσία του Ρονάλντο σε περίπου 1,4 δισεκατομμύρια δολάρια! Ασύλληπτο ποσό. Και πώς άραγε διαχειρίζεσαι τέτοια νούμερα; Ειδικά όταν μιλάμε για έναν άνθρωπο που, όπως θα λέγαμε για κάθε άλλον στη θέση του, ξέρει να κάνει ένα πράγμα καλύτερα από οτιδήποτε άλλο: να σκίζει δίχτυα. Ξέρει όμως και από επιχειρήσεις; Ο CR7 έχει σκεφτεί, προνοήσει και πράξει με υπερβάλλουσα διορατικότητα: δεν αντιμετωπίζει εδώ και πολλά χρόνια τη δημοσιότητά του απλώς ως πηγή διαφημιστικών συμβολαίων. Τη χρησιμοποιεί ως επιχειρηματικό κεφάλαιο, αποκτώντας συμμετοχές σε διαφορετικούς κλάδους. Η στρατηγική αυτή δεν εγγυάται επιτυχία, βεβαίως, καθώς οι επιχειρήσεις έχουν ρίσκο, οι αποτιμήσεις μεταβάλλονται και καμία επένδυση δεν… σκοράρει με την ευκολία και την εγγύηση σταθερότητας που σκόραρε εκείνος στα καλύτερά του χρόνια. Ο Ρονάλντο επιχειρεί να μετατρέψει μια ποδοσφαιρική καριέρα με ημερομηνία λήξης σε μια επιχειρηματική δραστηριότητα χωρίς προκαθορισμένο τελευταίο σφύριγμα. Γνωρίζει ότι κάποια μέρα (δεν αργεί πια, βιολογικά, όσο κι αν αυτός είναι «αγέραστος» στα γήπεδα) θα σταματήσει να σκοράρει. Το προφανές είναι πώς εκείνο που δεν σκοπεύει να σταματήσει είναι να κερδίζει… Διαβάστε επίσης: Διαβάστε επίσης: The post Ο πιο ακριβοπληρωμένος ποδοσφαιριστής του πλανήτη δεν αρκείται στα εκατομμύρια της μπάλας… appeared first on POPAGANDA .

items.title: Επιστήμονες ανακαλύπτουν νέα μορφή καρκίνου του προστάτη

items.descriptionOriginal: On a Saturday morning at a government school in Bengaluru's Mullur Colony, 17-year-old Asavari Agrawal barely gets through the gate before the children surround her. Some run up to hug her. Others tug at her hands, eager to show her something or pull her into a game. The younger ones often cling to her, refusing to let go even as she tries to begin the day's activities. By now, the scene is familiar. Asavari greets the teachers and children, gets everyone moving and settles into whatever the morning calls for. There may be table tennis, an art activity, a lesson, a fitness session or simply time spent talking and playing. "When she enters the gate, they run to her," says Victoria, headmistress of the school. "In the beginning they were shy. But because she came every week, they became comfortable very quickly." At 17, Asavari is balancing Class 12 , college applications, national-level table tennis, Bharatanatyam and Grade 8 piano. Yet for nearly five years, she has also made space for spending her weekends with children at government schools and residential homes across Bengaluru. For the children at Mullur Colony Government School, Saturday mornings mean games, activities and time with their favourite Didi. That commitment began when she was a child herself and eventually grew into Shape the Future, the youth-led initiative she founded at 13. Today, around 50 student volunteers are part of the wider network, reaching roughly 250 children. There have been sports sessions, health and eye camps, menstrual hygiene drives, book collections and learning activities. But when Asavari talks about what matters most, she does not begin with those numbers. "I think the idea of showing up is what matters most to my NGO," she says. "No matter how many drives or fundraisers or events that I hold, I feel like being there for the kids, emotionally and physically, matters the most." It started with playdates Asavari's connection with children from underserved communities began long before Shape the Future. When she was young, her mother began volunteering at Karuna Shreya hospice after experiencing several personal losses. Asavari would accompany her and, over time, also began visiting Thayi Mane, a government-recognised home for orphaned and destitute children. Back then, she did not think of herself as a volunteer. "I was really small when I started going there," she recalls. "Honestly, initially it was like playdates for me. It was so fun going there and playing with the kids." From table tennis and fitness sessions to art and learning activities, Asavari and her volunteers create opportunities for children to explore new interests. As she grew older, those visits began to look different. She started noticing the opportunities she had access to, from learning sports and dancing to playing the piano, and how different that access could be for the children she was meeting. In 2021, that realisation took a more concrete form. Asavari had started her own table tennis academy and decided to take the sport to the children she had been visiting. She brought tables, rackets, balls, shoes, clothes, jackets and fitness equipment and conducted a session for around 100 children. For many, table tennis was unfamiliar. "I think they were really excited to learn a new sport that they probably hadn't heard of yet," she says. The first session was not easy. Asavari was around the same age as many of the children and had to introduce a completely new sport to a large group. But some children took to it quickly, and the experience made her think about what else she could bring to them. Asavari believes that showing up consistently and building relationships with children matters more than organising one-off donation drives. A year later, in 2022, she started Shape the Future. What began with one sport slowly expanded into a broader effort to give children access to learning, play and experiences that might otherwise remain outside their everyday lives. What a Saturday looks like Today, a typical weekend begins with Asavari and her volunteers packing supplies for the day's session. Depending on the activity, that could mean sports equipment, stationery, educational material or art supplies. Around 10 to 15 volunteers may join her, although the group changes because they are all school students managing their own academic schedules. There is usually a warm-up, the main activity and plenty of time for games before everyone heads home. The session may last only a couple of hours, but it has become a regular part of Asavari's week. "I have a lot of exams and applications and personal work," she says. "But setting aside one or two hours every weekend doesn't do any harm. It's not like work to me. It's more of a hobby going there." With around 50 student volunteers, Shape the Future now reaches nearly 250 children across Bengaluru. At Mullur Colony, Victoria has seen that commitment first-hand. "Most Saturdays she comes herself. On some Saturdays when she cannot come, her team comes, but someone is always here every Saturday without fail," she says. That consistency has changed the relationship between Asavari and the children. "When she first came, they would just silently follow what she said," Victoria recalls. "Now they talk back, they argue, they pull her, they sit close to her. This closeness takes time. It comes only because she has been here every week." Aparna, in-charge and principal at Thayi Mane and Lakshya Residential School, has witnessed the same bond. "They know each one by name," she says. "They wait for her on Saturday. When she comes, they run to her." Why a missed Saturday matters to the children There are two kindergarten girls at Mullur Colony, Aarohi and Anjali, whom Asavari has grown particularly close to. When she arrives, they often run towards her and refuse to let go. "They keep calling me Didi, they keep calling me Amma," Asavari says. "We've built such a close connection with these kids that it just hurts me to not end up going there." For Asavari, the most meaningful part of volunteering is the trust she has built with children who now look forward to seeing her every Saturday. Then there is Sumit, a boy who recently lost both his parents. One day, he told Asavari, "You're the only family I have left now." For a teenager who is still learning how to understand grief, moments like this can be difficult to process. "I think I'm still too young to understand each and every kid's emotion," she says. "But I try." At Thayi Mane, Aparna remembers another moment. When Asavari had surgery on her appendix, she could not visit for several weeks. When she finally returned, a boy named Partha told her that one night his "heart pained" because he thought she might not come back. "She did not say anything. She just held him," Aparna recalls. These experiences have shaped Asavari's understanding of volunteering . She has seen people arrive for one-off activities, donate something, take photographs and leave. For children who have experienced people coming and going, that can make it difficult to trust that someone will stay. Sumit, who recently lost both his parents, found a sense of belonging in Asavari. "The best and worst part is getting attached to these kids," she says. The children have even told her that when she does not come, they worry she might leave like others have. "They don't look for money. They don't look for items," Asavari says. "They look for someone who isn't going to give up on them." For her, that means treating the children as equals rather than beneficiaries. "It's about not treating them like a project. Treating them as equals and constantly building that relationship." When the children asked for books The library at Mullur Colony grew out of these everyday conversations. Asavari would ask the children what they wanted to learn about, what they dreamed of becoming and what they wished they could read. Their answers revealed a simple gap: they wanted to explore beyond their school textbooks, but there were very few books available to them. So Asavari and her team began collecting them. Over nearly two years, five student volunteers took charge of the collection, reaching out to schools and communities and bringing in donated books. Slowly, the collection grew to more than 2,000. Asavari and her team transformed an unused room at the government school into a library, complete with bookshelves, furniture and reading material. The school also had a room that had essentially become a storage space. Turning it into a library meant redoing the flooring, repainting the walls, cleaning the room, adding shelves and furniture, and finally sorting and arranging the books. "It went from being an absolute rag of a room," Asavari says. "We had to uproot the entire flooring, repaint the walls, clean the entire room and then bring in the furniture and the books." For Victoria, who has watched the school change since Shape the Future first arrived in 2024, the library represents something the children simply did not have before. "Before this we had nothing. Only textbooks. No library, nothing like that," she says. "She collected more than two thousand books and arranged the room also with shelves and light. For our school this is a very big thing ." The idea has also been about understanding what individual children want to read rather than simply filling a room with books. At Thayi Mane, one girl wanted more advanced reading material, so Asavari sourced a set of 25 encyclopaedias specifically for her. "That kind of attention is rare," Aparna says. "The children feel seen when someone notices what they individually need." Preparing for the Saturdays she may miss Shape the Future has remained entirely bootstrapped. Asavari has funded its work through earnings from her Bharatanatyam Arangetram, table tennis prize money and even by selling her own piano and table tennis table. But she does not see those decisions as sacrifices. "I wouldn't call myself selfless," she says. "I think the kids needed it more than I did." If anything, the harder thing to give has been time. And now, time is precisely what Asavari is preparing to have less of. She is in Class 12 and hopes to study at university in the US or UK. For the first time since she began visiting these children regularly, she may soon be unable to walk through the school gates every Saturday. "I'm absolutely terrified as to how these kids are going to feel once I leave," she says. "When I'm in college, I'm not going to be able to come for months." So she is preparing Shape the Future to continue without her. Responsibilities have been divided among heads of fundraising, volunteering, social media and operations, while younger students are being given more responsibility. Asavari is deliberately preparing a team that can continue the work even when she is away. Her mother, who first introduced her to volunteering, remains part of that support system too. "This is not just Asavari's work," Aparna says. "Her mother has always been part of this. This is their family's commitment." Asavari describes what she hopes to build in a different way. "I think of it like generational wealth," she says. "You build it, you pass it on, you make sure it outlasts you." As she prepares to leave for university, Asavari is training younger volunteers to ensure Shape the Future continues even in her absence. What began as playdates now includes dozens of young volunteers, hundreds of children and a library built from thousands of donated books. Yet what Asavari values most cannot be measured in numbers. It is the familiarity of a Saturday morning, the children knowing she will walk through the gate, and the trust that has grown because she has kept returning. "I've just done it consistently," she says. "And I've grown it into something big. These little changes, being consistent with these little changes, is what matters most." Her advice to other young people is just as simple. "You don't need to build the world's biggest NGO. Start with 10 children, but stay." All images courtesy of Asavari Agrawal

items.descriptionOriginal: Ο Βασίλης Τσιατσιάμης, που πέρυσι είπε «δεν είμαι ο διαβήτης μου» εννοώντας ότι τη ζωή του δεν την ορίζει η ασθένεια, μιλά φέτος ως πατέρας, μετά τη διάγνωση της επτάχρονης κόρης του. Mε αφορμή την Παγκόσμια Ημέρα Διαβήτη , ο Βασίλης Τσιατσιάμης μίλησε στην κάμερα για τη ζωή του με τον διαβήτη και είπε τη φράση «δεν είμαι ο διαβήτης μου». Φέτος επιστρέφει με ένα νέο βίντεο ενός λεπτού, αυτή τη φορά ως πατέρας. Η κόρη του Λουίζα διαγνώστηκε με σακχαρώδη διαβήτη δύο μέρες μετά τα έβδομα γενέθλιά της. «Ζω είκοσι έξι χρόνια με διαβήτη και νόμιζα ότι τα ξέρω όλα. Την πρώτη νύχτα που σηκώθηκα για να μετρήσω το σάκχαρο της κόρης μου κατάλαβα ότι ξεκινούσα από την αρχή», λέει στο βίντεο ο δημιουργός του www.odiavitismou.gr . Το μήνυμά του έχει τρεις αποδέκτες. Στα παιδιά που έμαθαν φέτος «αυτή τη δύσκολη λέξη» λέει ότι είναι «πολύ πιο γενναία από όσα φαντάζονται» και τους υπόσχεται ότι «θα μεγαλώσετε, θα σβήσετε κεράκια, θα παίξετε και θα γίνετε ό,τι ονειρεύεστε» . Στη μαμά και τον μπαμπά που το βράδυ κοιμούνται με το ένα μάτι ανοιχτό απευθύνει μία φράση, «δεν έφταιγες εσύ σε τίποτα». Στους ενήλικες που ζουν χρόνια με διαβήτη θυμίζει ότι «ένα παιδί κάποια στιγμή σε κοιτάζει και μαθαίνει από σένα». Το βίντεο κλείνει με λίγα λόγια προς τη Λουίζα. «Έχουμε πολλή ζωή μπροστά μας και θα τη ζήσουμε μαζί όλοι», της λέει ο πατέρας της, και καταλήγει με την ευχή «για εμάς και τα παιδιά μας που ζούμε με τον διαβήτη, κάθε μέρα μετράει. Χρόνια μας πολλά». Η Παγκόσμια Ημέρα Διαβήτη τιμάται κάθε χρόνο στις 14 Νοεμβρίου. Το φετινό θέμα της Διεθνούς Ομοσπονδίας Διαβήτη (IDF) είναι η έγκαιρη δράση για τον διαβήτη. Στην Ελλάδα, σύμφωνα με στοιχεία που έχει ανακοινώσει η Πανελλήνια Ένωση Αγώνα κατά του Νεανικού Διαβήτη (ΠΕΑΝΔ), περισσότερα από 150 παιδιά διαγιγνώσκονται κάθε χρόνο με Σακχαρώδη Διαβήτη τύπου 1. items.descriptionOriginal: The advice for eating in a warming world is by now familiar: more beans, fruit and vegetables; less meat and dairy. But it seems the same plate could also help with an entirely different planetary problem. Two new studies in mice suggest that high-fiber diets help nanoplastics, the tiny plastic particles strewn through oceans and soils, and found in the food we eat, pass through the gut without being absorbed. High-fat diets, by contrast, appear to make the body hold onto more of them. Millions of tons of plastic waste enter the environment each year. This waste slowly degrades into microplastics and nanoplastics that find their way into farms, plants, ocean life, and even the Amazon—where they were recently found in the blood of wild tapirs and anteaters . Once ingested with food, these tiny particles percolate into the human brain, lungs, liver, kidneys, placenta, and testes , where they cause inflammation, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and other cellular injuries. Nanoplastics are even found in the atherosclerotic plaques of our coronary arteries , where they increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, or premature death by more than 4-fold. The two new studies looked at how diet influences the absorption and effects of nanoplastics in mice. One study found that in the first 24 hours after consuming nanoplastics, mice eating medium- or high-fiber diets accumulated two to seven times less plastics in their intestinal tract than those on regular diets. Mice fed nanoplastics for 28 days experienced inflammation and breakdown of their intestinal barriers—setting the stage for nanoplastics to enter the rest of the body; but these negative effects were absorption of nanoplastics by 2.8-fold compared to regular diets. That finding is especially worrisome, given that fast foods and takeout foods, both rich in fat, are often served in containers laced with plastics. In the two new studies, dietary fiber may have exerted its protective effects by shaping the intestinal microbiome, coating the nanoplastic particles, and speeding up their elimination through poop—allowing the intestinal lining to avoid excessive exposure. These new insights come at a time when scientists are already proposing higher-plant and lower-animal diets that could improve worldwide health while also reducing the environmental impacts of the global food system , such as greenhouse emissions, water pollution, and land use. Human studies are needed to confirm these newest results. But for the moment, they suggest that sustainable diets could also reduce another nasty problem: nanoplastics. items.descriptionOriginal: Δεκατέσσερις προσωπικές ιστορίες ανθρώπων που ζουν με σακχαρώδη διαβήτη τύπου 1 , καθώς και γονέων, εκπαιδευτικών και άλλων προσώπων του περιβάλλοντός τους, συγκεντρώνονται σε ένα νέο βιβλίο της Ελληνικής Ομοσπονδίας για τον Διαβήτη (ΕΛΟΔΙ ), το οποίο θα παρουσιαστεί τη Δευτέρα 16 Νοεμβρίου, στην Αθήνα. Το βιβλίο, με τίτλο « 14 Ιστορίες για τον Διαβήτη Τύπου 1 », καταγράφει διαφορετικές εμπειρίες από την καθημερινότητα με τη νόσο, αναδεικνύοντας τις προκλήσεις, τις αγωνίες, τις δυσκολίες αλλά και τις προσωπικές επιτυχίες των ανθρώπων που επηρεάζονται από αυτήν. Μέσα από τις αφηγήσεις, η ΕΛΟΔΙ επιδιώκει να αναδείξει τον αντίκτυπο του διαβήτη τύπου 1 πέρα από την ιατρική παρακολούθηση και τη θεραπευτική αντιμετώπισή του. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στις επιπτώσεις της νόσου στην οικογενειακή και κοινωνική ζωή, στην εκπαίδευση και στην προσωπική ανάπτυξη. Σύμφωνα με την Ομοσπονδία, η έκδοση εντάσσεται στις δράσεις ενημέρωσης και ευαισθητοποίησης για τον διαβήτη , με στόχο την καλύτερη κατανόηση των αναγκών των ανθρώπων που ζουν με τη νόσο και την αντιμετώπιση στερεοτύπων και προκαταλήψεων. Η παρουσίαση θα πραγματοποιηθεί τη Δευτέρα 16 Νοεμβρίου 2026, στις 18:00, στο Αμφιθέατρο «Αντώνης Τρίτσης» του Πνευματικού Κέντρου του Δήμου Αθηναίων, στην οδό Ακαδημίας 50, με είσοδο από τη Σόλωνος. Στην εκδήλωση αναμένεται να δοθεί έμφαση στις προσωπικές εμπειρίες των ανθρώπων που συμμετέχουν στο βιβλίο, με την ΕΛΟΔΙ να επισημαίνει ότι ο διαβήτης αποτελεί μέρος της ζωής τους, χωρίς να καθορίζει το σύνολο της ταυτότητάς τους. Διαβάστε επίσης Διαβήτης τύπου 2: Νέα θεωρία αλλάζει όσα ξέραμε για την αντίσταση στην ινσουλίνη Το αντιφλεγμονώδες ελληνικό βότανο που καταπολεμά διαβήτη και κατάθλιψη Περπάτημα: Ποια είναι η καλύτερη ώρα για τον έλεγχο του σακχάρου – Τι απαντούν οι ειδικοί

items.descriptionOriginal: Όλο και περισσότεροι άνθρωποι στρέφονται στα chatbots αναζητώντας συναισθηματική υποστήριξη ή συμβουλές για τις σχέσεις τους . Πόσο αξιόπιστες, όμως, είναι οι συμβουλές που λαμβάνουν και τι συμβαίνει όταν τα συγκεκριμένα εργαλεία συμφωνούν μαζί τους ακόμα κι όταν δεν θα έπρεπε; Η Alli Spotts-De Lazzer, ψυχοθεραπεύτρια, αποφάσισε να δοκιμάσει η ίδια την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη στον ρόλο του «θεραπευτή», πραγματοποιώντας ένα άτυπο προσωπικό πείραμα. Περιγράφοντας την εμπειρία της σε άρθρο της στο Psychology Today, αναγνωρίζει ότι ορισμένες απαντήσεις ήταν εντυπωσιακά καλές. Άλλες, ωστόσο, θα μπορούσαν να είχαν προκαλέσει σοβαρά προβλήματα στη σχέση για την οποία ζητούσε συμβουλές. Πόσο βοηθητική ήταν τελικά η συζήτηση; Η ψυχοθεραπεύτρια ξεκίνησε χρησιμοποιώντας το chatbot ως χώρο συναισθηματικής εκτόνωσης, ως έναν «κάδο απορριμμάτων των συναισθημάτων» όπως λέει χαρακτηριστικά. Εξέφρασε τον θυμό της , χωρίς να αποκαλύψει προσωπικά στοιχεία, ενώ στη συνέχεια ζήτησε βοήθεια για ένα πραγματικό πρόβλημα επικοινωνίας. Στόχος της ήταν να θέσει όρια σε ένα πρόσωπο του περιβάλλοντός της, αποφεύγοντας μια έντονη συναισθηματική αντίδραση ή μια νέα αντιπαράθεση. Η πρώτη απάντηση της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης ήταν γεμάτη κατανόηση και συναισθηματική επιβεβαίωση. «Αυτό ακούγεται τόσο επώδυνο!», της απάντησε, συνεχίζοντας με εκτενείς καθησυχαστικές διατυπώσεις. Ωστόσο, όπως διαπίστωσε, η υπερβολική επιβεβαίωση των συναισθημάτων της δεν συνοδευόταν από ουσιαστικά χρήσιμες συμβουλές . «Ομολογουμένως, η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ήταν καταπληκτική στο να επικυρώνει τα συναισθήματά μου. Ωστόσο, ευθυγραμμιζόταν υπερβολικά με αυτά και όχι με τους πραγματικούς μου στόχους» παρατηρεί. Όχι μόνο αυτό, αλλά το chatbot την ενθάρρυνε να χρησιμοποιήσει εκφράσεις που θα μπορούσαν να ακουστούν κατηγορητικές, αλλά και να παραθέσει πολλές λεπτομέρειες που πιθανότατα θα οδηγούσαν το άλλο πρόσωπο σε αμυντική στάση. «Οι συμβουλές για το τι θα μπορούσα να πω ενδέχεται να είχαν προκαλέσει σοβαρή ρήξη στη σχέση για την οποία ζητούσα βοήθεια», σχολιάζει. Η ίδια κατάφερε να αναγνωρίσει τα προβλήματα χάρη στην επαγγελματική της εκπαίδευση. Παρατήρησε, μάλιστα, ότι οι απαντήσεις βελτιώνονταν όταν έθετε πιο συγκεκριμένα ερωτήματα και ζητούσε από το εργαλείο Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης να εξετάσει διαφορετικές πιθανές αντιδράσεις. Στη συνέχεια, του έθεσε η ίδια μια πρόκληση. Όταν η ψυχοθεραπεύτρια αναφέρθηκε σε « ναρκισσιστικά χαρακτηριστικά » ενός προσώπου, το chatbot επέμεινε ότι δεν μπορούσε να θέσει διάγνωση, ακόμη κι όταν εκείνη διευκρίνισε ότι περιέγραφε συμπεριφορές και όχι κάποια ψυχική διαταραχή. «Ενώ φαινόταν να προσπαθεί να με κάνει να αισθανθώ ότι με καταλαβαίνει, την ίδια στιγμή ακύρωνε την εμπειρία μου», σημειώνει. Πότε η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη μπορεί να αποδειχθεί χρήσιμη Παρά τις επιφυλάξεις της, η Spotts-De Lazzer αναγνωρίζει ότι η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη μπορεί να λειτουργήσει ως εργαλείο βελτίωσης της επικοινωνίας και εξάσκησης της κριτικής σκέψης . Για παράδειγμα, όταν κάποιος είναι θυμωμένος, μπορεί να ζητήσει από ένα chatbot να διατυπώσει ένα μήνυμα με πιο ήπιο, ευγενικό ή ξεκάθαρο τρόπο. Αυτή η μικρή παύση πριν από την αποστολή ενός μηνύματος μπορεί να αποτρέψει μια παρορμητική αντίδραση για την οποία αργότερα θα μετανιώσει. Αυτό, όμως, δε σημαίνει ότι λειτουργεί τέλεια στην επικοινωνία, καθώς πολλές φορές δεν αντιλαμβάνεται τον σαρκασμό, τα υπονοούμενα ή την παθητικοεπιθετική συμπεριφορά. Γι’ αυτό, οι προτάσεις της χρειάζονται ανθρώπινη αξιολόγηση. Κυρίως, η χρήση της για απλά ζητήματα επικοινωνίας διαφέρει σημαντικά από την αναζήτηση συμβουλών για σοβαρά προβλήματα ψυχικής υγείας, όπου η υποστήριξη από κατάλληλα εκπαιδευμένους επαγγελματίες θεωρείται απαραίτητη. Πέντε συμβουλές για ασφαλέστερη χρήση της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης Η ψυχοθεραπεύτρια προτείνει πέντε βασικές πρακτικές για όσους χρησιμοποιούν chatbots σε προσωπικά ζητήματα: 1. Θυμηθείτε ότι δεν συνομιλείτε με άνθρωπο. Η ΤΝ μπορεί να παραβλέπει σημαντικές λεπτομέρειες και να συμφωνεί υπερβολικά μαζί σας. Μια καθησυχαστική απάντηση δεν είναι απαραίτητα και σωστή. 2. Εξηγήστε ξεκάθαρα τον στόχο σας. Αντί να ρωτήσετε απλώς «Τι να κάνω;», δοκιμάστε: «Θέλω να εκφράσω την απογοήτευσή μου χωρίς να προκαλέσω σύγκρουση. Πώς μπορώ να το πω;». 3. Ζητήστε να σας αμφισβητήσει. Ερωτήσεις όπως «Τι μπορεί να μου διαφεύγει;» ή «Πώς θα μπορούσε να ερμηνεύσει το άλλο πρόσωπο αυτή τη δήλωση;» μπορούν να σας βοηθήσουν να εξετάσετε διαφορετικές οπτικές. 4. Προστατεύστε τα προσωπικά σας δεδομένα. Αποφύγετε να μοιράζεστε ονόματα, διευθύνσεις και άλλες πληροφορίες που μπορούν να οδηγήσουν στην ταυτοποίηση τη δική σας ή τρίτων, χωρίς να γνωρίζετε πώς χρησιμοποιούνται. 5. Μην αντικαθιστάτε την ψυχοθεραπεία με την ΤΝ. Τα chatbots δεν μπορούν να υποκαταστήσουν την εξατομικευμένη κλινική αξιολόγηση, την ψυχολογική υποστήριξη και τη θεραπεία από επαγγελματίες ψυχικής υγείας. Το κρίσιμο ερώτημα: Μας βοηθά να σκεφτόμαστε ή μας λέει αυτό που θέλουμε να ακούσουμε; Η ψυχοθεραπεύτρια εξηγεί ότι πλέον συζητά ανοιχτά με τους θεραπευόμενούς της τη χρήση της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης. Όταν κάποιος αναφέρει ότι συμβουλεύτηκε ένα chatbot, τον ρωτά τι απάντηση έλαβε, πώς αισθάνθηκε και κατά πόσο τον βοήθησε. Όπως τονίζει, χρειάζεται να αξιολογούμε τις απαντήσεις της AI με την ίδια κριτική στάση που αντιμετωπίζουμε κάθε πληροφορία στο διαδίκτυο. «Για ορισμένα ζητήματα προσωπικής βελτίωσης ή επικοινωνίας, η AI μπορεί να αποδειχθεί χρήσιμη. Μπορεί, όμως, να προσφέρει και συμβουλές τις οποίες οι άνθρωποι εξακολουθούν να χρειάζεται να εξετάζουν, να αξιολογούν και να προσαρμόζουν στις δικές τους συνθήκες. Η εξάρτηση από την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ως υποκατάστατο της εξατομικευμένης φροντίδας ψυχικής υγείας μπορεί να αποδειχθεί πραγματικά επικίνδυνη» καταλήγει. Διαβάστε επίσης «Bixonimania»: Η νόσος που δεν υπήρξε ποτέ – Αλλά η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη την παρουσίασε ως αληθινή Η πικρή αλήθεια για την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη σε «ρόλο γιατρού» – Κάνει επικίνδυνα λάθη με μεγάλη αυτοπεποίθηση Τεχνητή νοημοσύνη και ψυχική υγεία: Μια νέα πραγματικότητα ανάμεσα σε αλγόριθμους και ανθρώπινες ανάγκες

items.descriptionOriginal: Ο σακχαρώδης διαβήτης είναι μία από τις μεγαλύτερες προκλήσεις για τη δημόσια υγεία παγκοσμίως. Ωστόσο, παρά το γεγονός ότι συχνά μιλάμε για τον διαβήτη σαν να πρόκειται για μία ενιαία νόσο, στην πραγματικότητα περιλαμβάνει διαφορετικές μορφές, με ξεχωριστούς μηχανισμούς εμφάνισης, διαφορετικά χαρακτηριστικά και διαφορετικές θεραπευτικές ανάγκες. Κοινός παρονομαστής όλων η υπεργλυκαιμία. Με αφορμή την Παγκόσμια Ημέρα Διαβήτη, στις 14 Νοεμβρίου 2026, η κυρία Σταυρούλα (Λίνα) Πάσχου, Αναπληρώτρια Καθηγήτρια Ενδοκρινολογίας ΕΚΠΑ, Υπεύθυνη Διαβητολογικού Κέντρου Νοσοκομείου ΑΛΕΞΑΝΔΡΑ αναδεικνύει τις παλαιότερες αλλά και τις νεότερες μορφές διαβήτη, επισημαίνοντας ότι η σωστή ταξινόμηση της νόσου αποτελεί βασική προϋπόθεση για την αποτελεσματική αντιμετώπισή της. Οι περισσότεροι γνωρίζουν τον διαβήτη τύπου 1 , ο οποίος οφείλεται σε αυτοάνοση καταστροφή των β κυττάρων του παγκρέατος που οδηγεί σε ανεπάρκεια ινσουλίνης, και τον πολύ συχνότερο διαβήτη τύπου 2, που συνδέεται κυρίως με παχυσαρκία, αντίσταση στην ινσουλίνη και σταδιακή δυσλειτουργία των β κυττάρων. Υπάρχουν, όμως, και άλλες μορφές που παραμένουν λιγότερο γνωστές. Μία από τις σημαντικότερες πρόσφατες εξελίξεις είναι η αναγνώριση του διαβήτη τύπου 5 , μιας μορφής διαβήτη που σχετίζεται με τον χρόνιο υποσιτισμό κατά την εφηβεία και τη νεαρή ενήλικη ζωή. Χαρακτηρίζεται από μειωμένη παραγωγή ινσουλίνης και εμφανίζεται κυρίως σε πληθυσμούς χωρών χαμηλού και μεσαίου εισοδήματος. Η Διεθνής Ομοσπονδία Διαβήτη (International Diabetes Federation – IDF) αναγνώρισε επίσημα αυτή την κατηγορία το 2025, ανοίγοντας ένα νέο κεφάλαιο στην κατανόηση της νόσου. Οι εκτιμήσεις κάνουν λόγο για περίπου 20–25 εκατομμύρια ανθρώπους που ενδέχεται να επηρεάζονται παγκοσμίως. Εξίσου σημαντικές είναι και άλλες ειδικές μορφές διαβήτη. Ο μονογονιδιακός διαβήτης, όπως ο MODY, ο οποίος οφείλεται σε γενετικές μεταβολές και συχνά εμφανίζεται σε νεαρή ηλικία, ο νεογνικός διαβήτης, καθώς και ο διαβήτης τύπου 3c, που σχετίζεται με παθήσεις ή βλάβες του παγκρέατος, όπως η χρόνια παγκρεατίτιδα ή η παγκρεατεκτομή. Επίσης, η βραδέως εξελισσόμενη αυτοάνοση μορφή διαβήτη στους ενήλικες, γνωστή παλαιότερα ως LADA, αποτελεί μια ιδιαίτερη κατηγορία που μπορεί αρχικά να συγχέεται με τον διαβήτη τύπου 2. Μια ακόμη σύγχρονη πρόκληση για την Ενδοκρινολογία είναι ο διαβήτης που προκαλείται από αντικαρκινικές θεραπείες. Η πρόοδος της Ογκολογίας και η χρήση καινοτόμων φαρμάκων έχουν βελτιώσει σημαντικά την επιβίωση πολλών ασθενών, ωστόσο ορισμένες θεραπείες μπορεί να επηρεάσουν τη λειτουργία του παγκρέατος ή τη ρύθμιση της γλυκόζης. Ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον παρουσιάζει ο διαβήτης που μπορεί να εμφανιστεί μετά τη χορήγηση ανοσοθεραπείας με αναστολείς των ανοσολογικών σημείων ελέγχου (immune checkpoint inhibitors), όπως η πεμπρολιζουμάμπη και η νιβολουμάμπη. Τα φάρμακα αυτά ενεργοποιούν το ανοσοποιητικό σύστημα εναντίον των καρκινικών κυττάρων, αλλά σε σπάνιες περιπτώσεις μπορεί να προκαλέσουν αυτοάνοση καταστροφή των β κυττάρων του παγκρέατος και αιφνίδια εμφάνιση σοβαρού, ινσουλινοεξαρτώμενου διαβήτη. Μάλιστα, η πρώτη εκδήλωση μπορεί να είναι η διαβητική κετοξέωση, μια δυνητικά απειλητική για τη ζωή επιπλοκή. Παράλληλα, ορισμένες στοχευμένες αντικαρκινικές θεραπείες , καθώς και τα κορτικοστεροειδή που χρησιμοποιούνται συχνά στην ογκολογία, μπορούν να προκαλέσουν σημαντική υπεργλυκαιμία ή να απορρυθμίσουν έναν ήδη υπάρχοντα διαβήτη. Για τον λόγο αυτό, η παρακολούθηση της γλυκόζης πριν, κατά τη διάρκεια και μετά τις αντικαρκινικές θεραπείες είναι ιδιαίτερα σημαντική. «Δεν είναι όλοι οι τύποι διαβήτη ίδιοι και δεν πρέπει να αντιμετωπίζονται όλοι με τον ίδιο τρόπο. Η σύγχρονη επιστημονική γνώση μας επιτρέπει να αναγνωρίζουμε διαφορετικούς μηχανισμούς πίσω από την ίδια κλινική εικόνα. Ένας άνθρωπος που έχει διαγνωστεί με διαβήτη τύπου 2 μπορεί, σε ορισμένες περιπτώσεις, να πάσχει στην πραγματικότητα από διαφορετική μορφή διαβήτη, όπως ο μονογονιδιακός διαβήτης ή η αυτοάνοση μορφή LADA. Αντίστοιχα, η εμφάνιση διαβήτη μετά από ανοσοθεραπεία απαιτεί διαφορετική προσέγγιση και στενή συνεργασία ενδοκρινολόγων και ογκολόγων. Η ακριβής διάγνωση δεν είναι απλώς θέμα ορολογίας – μπορεί να αλλάξει ουσιαστικά τη θεραπευτική αντιμετώπιση και την πορεία του ασθενούς», επισημαίνει η Σταυρούλα (Λίνα) Πάσχου, Αναπληρώτρια Καθηγήτρια Ενδοκρινολογίας ΕΚΠΑ. Η έγκαιρη διάγνωση παραμένει καθοριστική για όλες τις μορφές διαβήτη. Η αυξημένη δίψα, η συχνουρία, η ανεξήγητη κόπωση, η απώλεια βάρους και η θολή όραση είναι συμπτώματα που δεν πρέπει να αγνοούνται. Ιδιαίτερα στον διαβήτη τύπου 2, η νόσος μπορεί να εξελίσσεται για μεγάλο χρονικό διάστημα χωρίς εμφανή συμπτώματα, με αποτέλεσμα αρκετοί άνθρωποι να διαγιγνώσκονται όταν έχουν ήδη αναπτύξει επιπλοκές. Η συστηματική παρακολούθηση, ο προληπτικός έλεγχος των ατόμων υψηλού κινδύνου και κυρίως αυτών με παχυσαρκία, η υιοθέτηση υγιεινού τρόπου ζωής και η κατάλληλη θεραπευτική παρέμβαση μπορούν να μειώσουν σημαντικά τον κίνδυνο επιπλοκών, όπως τα καρδιαγγειακά νοσήματα, η χρόνια νεφρική νόσος, η διαβητική νευροπάθεια και αμφιβληστροειδοπάθεια. Το μήνυμα της Παγκόσμιας Ημέρας Διαβήτη 2026 είναι σαφές: Μαθαίνουμε να αναγνωρίζουμε τις διαφορετικές μορφές του διαβήτη, επενδύουμε στην έγκαιρη διάγνωση και αντιμετωπίζουμε κάθε ασθενή εξατομικευμένα. Γιατί πίσω από την ίδια λέξη μπορεί να κρύβονται διαφορετικές νόσοι και διαφορετικές ανάγκες. items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News A Year In, Networks for Nature is Reconnecting Cheshire’s Wild Spaces Reading Time: 3 minutes Chester Zoo’s Networks for Nature community project planted 14,000 trees and restored and created 13 ponds in its first year, putting it well on its way to its five-year goals. Networks for Nature started with a simple idea. Wildlife does better when habitats connect, and so do communities. One year in, about 8,700 people across northwest Cheshire, England, have put that idea to work. Chester Zoo launched the project with a £4.4 million grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund. It covers about 60 square miles, from Ellesmere Port to Chester, and runs through 2028. The Westminster Foundation and individual supporters also help fund it. The project builds on the zoo’s earlier Nature Recovery Corridor. That effort improved more than 62 hectares for wildlife and engaged over 12,000 people. Connection is the core of the approach. Small, isolated habitat patches leave plants and animals stranded. Hedgerows, ponds, and green corridors help them move, feed, and breed across a wider area. Hannah Brooks leads the project as Chester Zoo’s Senior Community Participation and Engagement Manager. She says connectivity is how species grow and thrive. In her view, the project works the same way, relying on landowners, community groups, and individuals working together. Networks for Nature’s first-year numbers show that cooperation in action. Volunteers and partners planted 14,000 trees and created or restored 13 ponds. They also established or restored 1.6 kilometers of hedgerow. Those figures put the project well on track. Over the full five years, it aims for 20 ponds and nearly 3,000 meters of hedgerow. In year one, it reached about two-thirds of the pond target and more than half of the hedgerow goal. Woodland work added nearly 7 hectares of new or improved habitat, roughly the size of 10 soccer fields. Teams also removed 269 tonnes of invasive plants and animals from the water. These species crowd out native wildlife and can choke waterways. One cleanup stands out. The project cleared 500 cubic meters of illegally dumped rubbish from a single community green space. That is enough to fill about seven large shipping containers. Each site has its own focus. At Gowy Meadows Nature Reserve near Ellesmere Port, work has improved public access. In Lache, a neglected space called The Backies has reopened as an enhanced community green space. Along the Shropshire Union Canal, teams have cleared invasive species. The Canal and River Trust is also monitoring water quality there. Meanwhile, The Land Trust is creating a wetland at Countess of Chester Country Park. Getting people to nature matters as much as restoring it. The project built 1,090 meters of new pathways so residents can reach green spaces more easily. Cheshire West and Chester Council is also planting wildflower meadows and improving five public parks for wildlife. Local participants did much of the hands-on work, from planting and clearing to laying footpaths. Others joined bug hunts, bird box building, and garden makeovers that brought wildlife closer to home. Some participants have gone further and trained as Wildlife Champions. They learn practical skills to keep improving outdoor spaces in their own neighborhoods. Brooks sees this long-term local leadership as central to the project’s value. Young people have played a central role. In year one, 83 young people joined hedgehog awareness campaigns, built bird and bat boxes, and improved allotments. They also completed leadership skills courses, nearly reaching the project’s five-year goal of 90. Schools are the next big focus for Networks for Nature. The project aims to reach 4,500 students through a year-long program to improve school grounds for wildlife. Local pupils have already joined in through wildlife clubs. Through Networks for Nature, Sutton Green Primary pupils joined the City Nature Challenge, using tablets to log the plants and animals they found outdoors. Photo courtesy of Chester Zoo . The project also links nature with health. Through green social prescribing, doctors can refer patients to outdoor, nature-based activities instead of, or alongside, medicine. Western Avenue Medical Centre in Blacon and Great Sutton Medical Centre in Ellesmere Port take part. Research suggests that time in green spaces can boost mental and physical wellbeing. Restoring parks and ponds close to home makes that benefit easier for residents to reach. Helen Featherstone, Director, England, North at The National Lottery Heritage Fund, praised the project’s community-led approach. She says it shows how communities and conservation groups can protect natural heritage together for the long term. Year one has focused on completed work, such as planting trees and restoring ponds. The bigger test will be whether wildlife responds. Ongoing monitoring, including water quality checks on the canal, will help show those results over time. The first year shows what community involvement adds. Thousands of residents turned a funded plan into trees in the ground, cleaner green spaces, and new local leaders. With four years still to go, Networks for Nature is only beginning to grow. Schools, community groups, landowners, and volunteers can learn more on Chester Zoo’s Networks for Nature page. Opportunities to train and take part continue to expand. The post A Year In, Networks for Nature is Reconnecting Cheshire’s Wild Spaces appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Your height is one number. Your weight is another. Put them together and you get your BMI. But is that enough to understand your weight and health? Not by itself. BMI is a useful screening measure. But it doesn’t directly tell us how much of your weight is muscle or fat, or where that fat is stored. That is where your waist adds context, giving us a view of abdominal fat distribution that can be relevant to cardiometabolic risk. So should you trust your waist more than your BMI? Not really. They give different information, and neither is a diagnosis on its own. If they seem to tell different stories, don’t try to diagnose yourself. Bring both to a qualified doctor. Use them as a reason to have a conversation, not to judge yourself. Keep up balanced meals, regular movement, strength activity and good sleep. BMI and waist are starting points, not verdicts. Talk to a qualified doctor about your weight-management needs. This is general information, not a diagnosis or medical advice. #CountWhatMatters #BMI #WaistMeasurement #KnowYourNumbers #MetabolicHealth [BMI vs waist measurement, what does BMI tell you, is BMI enough, waist size and health risk, body composition India]

items.descriptionOriginal: Every winter, Delhi struggles with worsening air pollution . As smog settles over the city, efforts to clear the air raise an unusual possibility. What if it rained? Could artificial rain wash away pollutants and make the air easier to breathe? The idea gained attention after the United Arab Emirates (UAE) invested in cloud seeding, a technique that encourages existing clouds to produce rainfall. Research in the region has also highlighted how rain can reduce airborne dust and particulate matter. This raised hopes that the same technology could help Delhi tackle its pollution. In October 2025, the Delhi government partnered with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur to conduct a cloud-seeding experiment. However, the operation failed to produce meaningful rainfall in the capital. So, why did a technique associated with improved air quality in Dubai fail in Delhi? The answer lies in differences in weather conditions, cloud formation, and the limitations of cloud seeding. What happened in Dubai? The UAE has invested in cloud seeding for decades to increase rainfall in a country that receives very little natural precipitation. Its programme primarily aims to improve water security and replenish groundwater. Every winter, Delhi struggles with worsening air pollution. Photograph: (Image generated by AI) Researchers have also examined whether rainfall could help reduce air pollution in the region. A study published in the journal Environmental Pollution examined atmospheric dust and particulate matter around Dubai and Abu Dhabi. It found that dust storms contributed to higher concentrations of suspended particles, while rainfall helped bring these levels down. A January 2021 report by The National highlighted these findings. When raindrops fall through the atmosphere, they collect suspended particles and carry them towards the ground. This process, known as wet deposition, helps remove some pollutants from the air. However, the research established the benefits of rainfall in reducing airborne dust. It did not conclusively prove that cloud seeding alone was responsible for improving Dubai's air quality. How does cloud seeding work? Cloud seeding does not create clouds or produce rain from a clear sky. It works by introducing tiny particles into existing clouds to encourage water droplets or ice crystals to grow. Depending on the cloud type and atmospheric conditions, scientists use materials such as silver iodide or salts, including sodium chloride and potassium chloride. These particles act as nuclei around which water droplets or ice crystals form . As the droplets grow heavier, they may eventually fall as rain. The UAE uses specially equipped aircraft to release seeding materials into suitable clouds. However, the technique needs naturally occurring clouds with sufficient moisture. According to the World Meteorological Organization , cloud seeding cannot create rain clouds or bring moisture into an otherwise dry atmosphere. Cloud seeding does not create clouds or produce rain from a clear sky. Photograph: (Reuters) Why did the experiment fail in Delhi? On 28 October 2025, aircraft carrying cloud-seeding flares conducted two sorties over parts of Delhi, including Burari, Karol Bagh, and Mayur Vihar. The experiment was part of a pilot project undertaken by the Delhi government in collaboration with IIT Kanpur. However, it did not produce rainfall in Delhi. Only negligible precipitation was recorded in neighbouring Noida and Greater Noida, at 0.1 mm and 0.2 mm respectively. The biggest obstacle was insufficient moisture in the clouds. According to NDTV's report on the experiment , IIT Kanpur director Manindra Agarwal explained that the clouds had moisture levels of around 15 to 20 percent, which were insufficient to trigger the desired rainfall. A second attempt scheduled for 29 October was also put on hold because atmospheric conditions were unsuitable. The problem was not simply the technology or the material released by the aircraft. The clouds themselves lacked the conditions needed to produce rain. Delhi's winter weather adds to the challenge Delhi's weather makes cloud seeding particularly difficult during the months when pollution is at its worst. During winter, the city frequently experiences low wind speeds, temperature inversions, and limited atmospheric mixing. These conditions trap pollutants close to the ground instead of allowing them to disperse. At the same time, the atmosphere often lacks the moisture and suitable cloud formations required for artificial rainfall. A study by IIT Delhi researchers titled 'Can Cloud Seeding Help Tackle Delhi's Air Pollution?' examined weather and pollution data collected between 2011 and 2021. The researchers found that suitable conditions for cloud seeding are relatively uncommon during Delhi's winter pollution season. Western disturbances, which bring moisture and precipitation to north-western India, can occasionally create favourable conditions. However, these opportunities are limited. The researchers concluded that cloud seeding could be considered an emergency measure when suitable weather conditions exist, but it cannot serve as a dependable pollution-control strategy. Can artificial rain really clear the air? Rainfall can help remove suspended particles, but the relief is generally temporary. Depending on the cloud type and atmospheric conditions, scientists use materials such as silver iodide or salts, including sodium chloride and potassium chloride. Photograph: (Newsonair) The IIT Delhi research found that heavy rainfall can wash out PM2.5 and PM10 more effectively than light rainfall. However, pollutant concentrations can return to earlier levels within one to five days as vehicles, industries, and other sources continue releasing emissions. Delhi's pollution comes from several sources, including vehicular exhaust, construction dust, industrial emissions, waste burning, and agricultural residue burning. Even if cloud seeding successfully produces rain, it cannot stop these sources from adding fresh pollutants to the atmosphere. There is also no conclusive evidence that cloud seeding consistently improves air quality in every region. A 2022 study published in the International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology examined particulate matter during cloud-seeding operations in the UAE and raised questions about the possible contribution of seeding materials to airborne particles. What does this mean for Delhi? Dubai's experience shows how rainfall can help remove airborne dust, but it does not establish cloud seeding as a reliable way to reduce AQI. Delhi's failed experiment highlights an important limitation. Technology can encourage clouds to produce rain, but it cannot compensate for unsuitable weather conditions. On 28 October 2025, aircraft carrying cloud-seeding flares conducted two sorties over parts of Delhi, including Burari, Karol Bagh, and Mayur Vihar. Photograph: (India Weekly) Cloud seeding may offer temporary relief when sufficient moisture and suitable clouds are available. For Delhi, cleaner air will depend less on waiting for artificial rain and more on preventing pollutants from entering the atmosphere in the first place. Better control of vehicle emissions, construction dust, industrial pollution, and agricultural burning will do far more for long-term air quality than waiting for the right clouds to arrive.

items.descriptionOriginal: Grief has a way of ambushing us in ordinary places. It was in the middle of an Ikea store, surrounded by display of sofas and couples building lives together, that a recently widowed woman sat down and wept. A passing stranger stopped, pressed a packet of tissues into her hands, rested a palm on her shoulder, and waited in silence until a nod signaled she was steadier. Then, she simply walked on. That wordless exchange, offered without expectation or introduction, cracked something open: "I knew then that a relationship was possible, because there are good people in the world." What followed, over the next decade, was a new love, a rebuilt life, and a quiet personal ritual -- the widow now carries tissues wherever she goes and has pressed them into the hands of four strangers crying in restaurants and bars. Kindness, it turns out, doesn't just comfort; it teaches, and those who receive it often become its most faithful carriers.

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Living with the Wild Documentary Confronts What Coexistence Actually Looks Like Reading Time: 3 minutes A five-part Living with the Wild documentary series explores what coexistence really looks like as elephants, lions, and rural communities increasingly compete for the same shrinking landscapes. Living with the Wild documentary from the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) arrives at a moment when human-wildlife conflict has become one of conservation’s most pressing and least resolved challenges. Across Africa’s great ecosystems, growing human populations, expanding agriculture, and shifting climate patterns push people and wildlife into ever-closer proximity, often with deadly consequences for both. Nowhere is this tension more visible than in Kenya’s Amboseli ecosystem, a landscape spanning the shadow of Mount Kilimanjaro where more than a thousand elephants roam alongside tens of thousands of Maasai pastoralists and their livestock. The documentary draws heavily on landscapes like this, where elephants raiding crops can destroy an entire family’s harvest overnight, and where retaliatory killings of wildlife remain a persistent, painful reality. IFAW has worked in Amboseli for years, partnering with the Amboseli Ecosystem Trust and Kenya Wildlife Service to mitigate conflict and secure migratory corridors elephants depend on. The organization’s multi-year commitment to securing tens of thousands of acres as wildlife dispersal land reflects a core premise underlying the Living with the Wild documentary: coexistence requires physical space, not just goodwill. That space-based approach extends well beyond Amboseli through IFAW’s broader Room to Roam initiative, which works to secure safe migratory corridors for African elephants across multiple countries. In Zimbabwe, the initiative has leased tens of thousands of acres between Victoria Falls and Hwange National Park, creating no-poaching territory that benefits elephants and more than a dozen other migratory species sharing the landscape. The Living with the Wild documentary connects to IFAW’s Room to Roam initiative, which secures tens of thousands of acres of safe migratory territory for elephants and other species across Southern Africa, demonstrating how physical space underpins genuine coexistence. Photo by Gil DAIX on Pexels. The Living with the Wild documentary captures a central truth about modern conservation: protecting iconic species increasingly means addressing the needs of the people living alongside them, not treating human and wildlife welfare as competing priorities. Communities bordering protected areas often bear disproportionate costs from wildlife presence, losing crops, livestock, and sometimes lives, while receiving comparatively little benefit from the tourism revenue wildlife generates elsewhere. Addressing this imbalance requires solutions extending beyond fences and patrols. IFAW’s work supporting human-wildlife conflict mitigation has included deploying tracking collars on elephants to better predict and prevent dangerous encounters, funding infrastructure improvements benefiting local communities, and developing early warning systems that help people and elephants avoid confrontations before they escalate into tragedy. The Living with the Wild documentary arrives as momentum builds to treat coexistence as an achievable policy rather than a distant aspiration. Organizations including the Elephant Protection Initiative increasingly bring communities, governments, and conservation groups to the same table, recognizing that sustainable solutions require buy-in from everyone sharing a landscape, not interventions imposed from outside. This shift matters because conventional conservation approaches, focused narrowly on anti-poaching enforcement or protected-area boundaries, often fail to address why conflict happens in the first place. When communities lose half their crops to wildlife and receive no compensation or support for alternative livelihoods, tolerance for coexistence erodes, no matter how much international attention a species receives. The Living with the Wild documentary suggests that genuine coexistence depends on reframing wildlife not as a burden communities must endure, but as a shared resource whose benefits and costs are distributed more equitably. Corridors that allow elephants to migrate safely also reduce crop-raiding incidents. Conflict mitigation infrastructure protects both human livelihoods and animal lives. Community-based conservation models increasingly demonstrate that when local people have genuine stakes in wildlife survival, coexistence becomes self-reinforcing rather than externally enforced. As climate change intensifies pressure on already-strained landscapes and pushes wildlife and communities into more frequent contact, the questions raised throughout the Living with the Wild documentary will only grow more urgent. The series offers no simple resolution, because none exists. Instead, it offers a clear-eyed look at what sharing a planet with megafauna requires: space, compromise, and sustained investment in solutions that work for both the elephants crossing ancient migratory routes and the families whose homes and farms lie along the way. The post Living with the Wild Documentary Confronts What Coexistence Actually Looks Like appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.titleOriginal: From Russia to Bengal's Coast: The Journey of a Critically Endangered Spoon-Billed Sandpiper
items.description: Αυτή η ιστορία είναι μέρος της νέας σειράς άγριας ζωής The Better India, Species in Focus: 52 species. 52 ιστορίες. 52 λόγοι για να προστατεύσετε την άγρια ​​ζωή της Ινδίας. Ένα λάιμ-πράσινο δαχτυλίδι με την ένδειξη '2K' βοήθησε β…
items.descriptionOriginal: This story is part of The Better India's new wildlife series, Species in Focus: 52 species. 52 stories. 52 reasons to protect India's wildlife. One species at a time, the series explores India's rare, endangered and lesser-known wildlife, their habitats, behaviour, ecological roles and conservation status. A lime-green ring marked '2K' has helped birdwatchers in Bengal identify a visitor whose journey began thousands of kilometres away. The bird, a spoon-billed sandpiper, was photographed at Kargil Beach in Bakkhali, South 24 Parganas, on October 24, 2026. The following day, it was spotted again at nearby Patibunia Beach. According to The Times of India , the bird was tagged in Russia's Chukotka region on July 6, 2025. Its appearance on the Bengal coast, around 8,000 km from its tagging location, offers a glimpse into the movements of one of the world's most threatened migratory shorebirds. For birdwatchers, identifying the same individual across different locations is an important record. The spoon-billed sandpiper's survival is tied to a chain of coastal habitats stretching from the Russian Far East to South and Southeast Asia. Bengal is one part of this journey, and protecting its mudflats matters far beyond the state's coastline. A tag that connects two coastlines The bird's movements along the Bengal coast have been documented over several months. On March 29, 2026, birdwatcher Sandip Das, a founding member of the Bengal-based Birdwatchers' Society, photographed a spoon-billed sandpiper at Patibunia Beach. Birdwatchers Soumya Aon and Kaustav Khan were also present. Two days later, another individual was photographed by Jayanta Manna. This second bird carried a lime-green tag on its right leg . The tagged bird continued to be sighted at Patibunia until June 1. When it reappeared at Kargil Beach in October, the tag marked '2K' helped birdwatchers establish that it was the same individual. The bird may be only a few centimetres long, but its journey links conservation decisions across continents. Photograph: (Facebook/BirdCount India) According to Das, the bird may have travelled to feeding grounds in Bangladesh before returning to Bengal. He also told The Times of India that a return to its Russian breeding site was unlikely, as the territory was already occupied by breeding pairs , potentially leading to conflict. With these sightings, three individual spoon-billed sandpipers have now been photographically recorded in Bengal: one in 2018 and two in 2026. But what makes this record important is not simply that a rare bird has visited the state. It offers evidence of how individual birds move between habitats, helping researchers understand which coastal stretches they depend on. Why a spoon-shaped bill matters Unlike most sandpipers, which have relatively straight, narrow bills, this species has a distinctive spatula-shaped tip that helps it pick small food items from wet mud. These birds feed on small invertebrates and other organisms found in intertidal mudflats. Such habitats provide food and resting places during migration, helping them build the energy needed to continue their journey. The species is classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List. Its global wild population is estimated at fewer than 500 individuals. The challenge is that its feeding grounds are not interchangeable. A bird that loses access to one important stopover may not find another suitable habitat in time. When a wetland disappears, the journey is interrupted The spoon-billed sandpiper's migration takes it across the East Asian–Australasian Flyway, a network of routes connecting breeding grounds in the north with wintering areas further south. One of its most important ecological bottlenecks is the Yellow Sea, between China and the Korean Peninsula. Its tidal flats provide feeding and resting grounds for migratory shorebirds. 🏁It's time for the birds' annual migration marathon 🕊️ 🐧 🦅 Watch this video to follow a remarkable spoon-billed sandpiper's incredible journey over thousands of kilometres. Will he be able to cross the finish line? #SaveSpoonie #wetlands #WMBD2023 #wwfindia #wwf https://t.co/eyY4devKST — WWF-India (@WWFINDIA) May 13, 2023 However, coastal reclamation, infrastructure development, hunting and disturbance have reduced or degraded several of these habitats. In June 2026, Sixth Tone , a Chinese news daily, reported how public pressure helped halt a proposed highway in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. The 47-km project, estimated to cost 5.1 billion yuan (approximately $710 million), threatened mudflats used by nearly 20,000 waterbirds belonging to 46 species. An environmental assessment identified more than 24 hectares of important spoon-billed sandpiper habitat, including mangrove wetlands . Following citizen campaigns and complaints to authorities, China's central environmental authorities suspended the project on May 25, finding that its environmental assessment lacked a sufficient scientific basis. Alternative routes were subsequently proposed for evaluation. Can conservation give the species a head start? One conservation intervention being used in Russia is called headstarting. Under this method, eggs are collected from the wild, incubated and hatched under human care. The chicks are raised until they are old enough to be released into their natural habitat. According to the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT), 236 headstarted spoon-billed sandpipers have been released so far, with 19 subsequently returning to breed in Russia. Illustrated by @mitul987 and Asif Kureshi. The Spoon-billed Sandpiper is listed as critically #endangered by @IUCNRedList. Fewer than 200 estimated in the #wild, It's never been recorded breeding over 5 km from the shore. Destruction of #wetlands is a huge threat to this #bird. https://t.co/WnYMtpAU4r — Sanctuary Asia (@SanctuaryAsia) December 10, 2019 The technique addresses one of the species' biggest challenges: the low survival rate of chicks in the wild. WWT estimates that only around three out of every 20 eggs laid naturally produce chicks that survive to adulthood, compared with 15 out of every 20 among headstarted chicks. However, breeding interventions cannot replace the need to protect the wetlands these birds depend on. What Bengal's sightings mean Back in Bakkhali, conservation efforts are also taking place at the local level. Birdwatchers have been conducting monthly surveys at Patibunia and Kargil beaches to monitor waders and other shorebirds. The South 24 Parganas Forest Department has installed signboards asking visitors and local residents not to disturb birdlife and has increased patrolling. The appearance of bird '2K' does not, by itself, indicate that the spoon-billed sandpiper population is recovering. But it provides another record of the connections between Bengal's coastline and distant breeding and feeding grounds. The bird may be only a few centimetres long, but its journey links conservation decisions across continents. Whether it can make that journey again will depend, in part, on whether places like Bakkhali remain safe enough for it to stop, feed and move on. Sources: 'Critically endangered Spoon-billed Sandpiper, tagged in Russia, sighted again on Bengal beach' : By TOI, Published on 26 October 2026 'Critically endangered spoon-billed sandpiper clicked on beach near Bakkhali, 2nd photo record from Bengal' : Krishnendu Mukherjee, Published on 30 March 2026 'How a Rare Bird Stopped a Highway Project in South China' : By Jiang Xinyi and Yang Yang, Published on 2 June 2026

items.description: Φανταστείτε να ξοδεύετε χρόνια παρακολουθώντας ταινίες και να αναρωτιέστε πώς φτιάχνονται, για να βρείτε το δικό σας όνομα στους τίτλους τέλους ενός! Αυτή είναι η σουρεαλιστική στιγμή για τον Mani Kantesh Allapuram, του οποίου το δημιουργικό ταξίδι ξεκίνησε με μερικές επεξεργασίες βίντεο και πολλή περιέργεια. Ο πατέρας του τον μύησε στην επεξεργασία βίντεο στην τάξη 11. Σύντομα, η Μάνη έκανε επεξεργασίες, σχεδιάζοντας το g…
items.descriptionOriginal: Imagine spending years watching films and wondering how they’re made, only to find your own name in the end credits of one! That’s the surreal moment for Mani Kantesh Allapuram, whose creative journey began with a few video edits and a lot of curiosity. His father introduced him to video editing in Class 11. Soon, Mani was making edits, designing graphics, and putting his ideas online, simply because he loved creating. During the lockdown, he took that passion further, spending hours experimenting with creative tools. Even while pursuing Computer Science, he kept finding ways to explore visual storytelling. And those experiments eventually opened a door he hadn’t imagined. His work caught the attention of DNEG, one of the world’s leading visual effects studios. He joined the team in early 2026 as a Creative Technology Artist and got the opportunity to contribute to Ramayana. For someone who once watched films dreaming about the magic behind them, being credited alongside some of the industry’s finest artists, including A. R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer, is a full-circle moment. As Mani says, “Your boy made it to the big screen.” A reminder that the things you create just for the love of it might one day take you somewhere extraordinary. #Ramayana #BehindTheScenes #RamayanaVFX #VisualEffects #IndianCinema #RamayanaMovie #7yearsforramayan #makingoframayan

items.titleOriginal: Artist reimagines the Beatles’ ‘Don’t Let Me Down’ as a modern rock song and people are demanding a full album
items.description: Στις αρχές της δεκαετίας του 2000, οι επιτυχίες των Beatles θεωρούνταν παλιές και παίζονταν κυρίως σε ραδιοφωνικούς σταθμούς. Σήμερα; Είναι άλλα είκοσι χρόνια μεγαλύτεροι. Είναι εύκολο να δεις τους Beatles σαν τα πρόσωπα στο Mount Rushmore: εμβληματικά και ιστορικά σημαντικά, αλλά όχι πλέον σχετικά. Αυτό που λείπει από πολλούς είναι η διαχρονική ποιότητα της τραγουδοποιίας των Beatles.…
items.descriptionOriginal: In the early 2000s, The Beatles ‘ hits were considered oldies and mostly played on throwback radio stations. Today? They’re another twenty years older. It’s easy to see The Beatles like the faces on Mount Rushmore: iconic and historically important, but no longer relevant. What many people miss is the timeless quality of The Beatles’ songwriting . While the sound and production of their music hark back to a bygone era, the lyrics and emotion could never go out of style. Sometimes it just takes listening in a new way to hear it. Artist covers The Beatles in a modern rock style Alex Melton is a popular musician and content creator with over 510,000 subscribers on his YouTube channel. He’s built a rabid following with wildly creative covers, often putting a pop-punk or 2000s spin on everything from pop to country to even a few oldies. He recently dug up a classic Beatles tune, “Don’t Let Me Down,” and reimagined it for the 21st century. He brings it to life in his very own way with electric guitar, sweet drum fills, and surprise key changes. The result is reminiscent of Switchfoot, Finger Eleven, Foo Fighters, and many other influential 2000s rock bands. It’s a must-listen. Listeners and viewers are clamoring for the full album Originally released on the B-side of The Beatles’ hit single “Get Back,” “Don’t Let Me Down” is a cult favorite. Melton’s electrifying cover is sparking nostalgia among Beatles fans and maybe even wooing some new ones. Commenters flooded Melton’s video with praise: “Now we need a Beatles covers album” “So stoked for this one!! More Beatles pls!!” “As a 35 year old who also just got into the Beatles and watched Get Back, I am SO here for this. Don’t Let Me Down and I’ve Got A Feeling are two of my favorites from them.” “Oh boy, I could use a whole EP of these!” “This is how you can tell that doing a cover is an art of its own. This echoes of the original in a way that feels instantly familiar and yet entirely brand new. This is how you cover a Beatles song.” “It’s never too late to get into a Beatles phase, more power to ya!” Melton writes in his YouTube channel description that, at 36, he never had much interest in The Beatles beyond a distant appreciation for their musical contributions. But the 2021 documentary Get Back , directed by Peter Jackson, sucked him in. “The four guys were so compelling and charming and funny and not afraid to be artists,” he writes. “So now I’m in my Beatles phase, at 36 years old.” Sometimes a new spin and a fresh interpretation are exactly what a new audience needs to appreciate the brilliance of the original more deeply. The post Artist reimagines the Beatles’ ‘Don’t Let Me Down’ as a modern rock song and people are demanding a full album appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: A professor asked students where they saved their work. Some didn’t understand the question.
items.description: Η καθηγήτρια μηχανικής Catherine Garland ρώτησε τους μαθητές της πού είχαν αποθηκεύσει τα αρχεία του υπολογιστή τους και κάποιοι δεν κατάλαβαν τι εννοούσε. Ήταν άνετοι χρησιμοποιώντας υπολογιστές, αλλά η οργάνωση αρχείων σε φακέλους και καταλόγους ήταν άγνωστη σε ορισμένους. Η εμπειρία του Garland παρουσιάστηκε σε ένα άρθρο του 2021 The Verge σχετικά με ένα εκπληκτικό κενό στους νέους…
items.descriptionOriginal: Engineering professor Catherine Garland asked her students where they’d saved their computer files , and some didn’t understand what she meant. They were comfortable using computers , but organizing files into folders and directories was unfamiliar to some. Garland’s experience was featured in a 2021 The Verge article about a surprising gap in young people’s computer skills. Although many students have grown up using smartphones, tablets, and laptops, that doesn’t necessarily mean they understand how files are stored and organized. Working on a laptop at school. Photo Credit: Canva Why do some students struggle to find their files? The problem first caught Garland’s attention in 2017 while she was teaching an engineering course. Students were using software to simulate jet-engine turbines. Some encountered error messages because the program couldn’t locate their files. Garland tried to help by asking where they’d saved their work. Had they put it on the desktop? Was it on a shared drive? Some students didn’t understand the questions. As Garland explained in The Verge article, “They see it like one bucket, and everything’s in the bucket.” Other instructors described similar experiences. Lincoln Colling, a psychology lecturer at the University of Sussex, recalled asking students to retrieve a file from a specific directory, only to be met with blank stares. Nicolás Guarín-Zapata , an applied physicist and lecturer at Universidad EAFIT in Colombia, also noticed students struggling to find their documents. He began teaching basic computer organization at the start of each semester, including how files and folders work. Older computer interfaces often required users to navigate through folders to locate their work. Today, search functions and apps can make that process largely unnecessary. Someone can open a document without ever thinking about which folder contains it. That convenience can become a problem when students encounter software that requires them to know exactly where a file is stored. Young students in an innovative robotics class. Photo Credit: Canva Growing up with technology doesn’t mean knowing everything about it A 2026 study published in the Journal of Statistics and Data Science Education examined computer literacy among university students taking introductory statistical programming courses in Germany. Researchers found considerable differences in students’ computer experience and confidence with everyday tasks. Most students felt comfortable creating documents, downloading files, and using search engines. But confidence was less consistent for tasks such as managing files, installing programs, and using operating-system search functions. Although nearly all students used smartphones daily, their experience with desktop computers varied considerably. The findings suggest that regularly using digital devices doesn’t necessarily make students confident with every computer task. A teacher helping students on the computer. Photo Credit: Canva Teaching the skills students haven’t learned Agnes Cameron , a specialist technician at the University of the Arts London’s Creative Computing Institute, developed workshops to help students build basic computer skills. According to her January 2026 teaching case study , the workshops included practical activities involving image editing and web design. They were designed to help students become more comfortable using computers and the software required for their coursework. A “New skills” button on a computer keyboard. Photo Credit: Canva A simple computer skill that can make life easier Fortunately, the basics of file organization are fairly simple. A file is a document or piece of information saved on a computer. A folder holds files and can contain other folders. A file path identifies the location of a particular file within that structure. For example, a student saves an assignment inside a folder named “Schoolwork,” which sits inside their “Documents folder.” Knowing that location makes it easier to find the assignment later, especially if the application asks them to select a particular file. Garland eventually began rethinking her own approach to organizing files. She started using her computer’s search function to find schedules and documents instead of navigating through folders. “I’m like, huh … I don’t even need these subfolders,” Garland said.
